hints.text: Multiply the digits as if there were no decimal points. The total number of decimal places in the two factors goes into the product.
Work out $4 \times 5$. Then count places: $0.4$ has one and $0.05$ has two, so the product needs three decimal places. You may need a zero in front as a placeholder.
$4 \times 5 = 20$, and with three decimal places this is $0.020$, which equals $0.02$.

explanation: Ignore the decimal points first and multiply the digits: $4 \times 5 = 20$.
Count the decimal places in the factors: $0.4$ has $1$ and $0.05$ has $2$, for a total of $3$.
Write $20$ with three decimal places. A zero is needed in front as a placeholder, giving $0.020$.
The final zero can be dropped, so the product is $0.02$.
